text:
Taylor: hey team, onboarding oddball. setting up a loaner Mac for our booth (kiosk mode) and ran into a FileVault/auto-login conflict. Kandji policy says FileVault must be On, but the kiosk needs automatic login to a managed account. macOS won't let me enable auto-login when FileVault is on. any safe path?
marco-it: welcome Taylor! yep thats expected. Auto-login is blocked by FileVault because it would store the password plaintext on disk. For kiosks we usually either: 1) supervise the device and apply a managed profile that exempts it from FileVault enforcement, then enable a managed auto-login, or 2) keep FileVault and use a launch agent that starts the kiosk app after login by a manually unlocked session (but that requires someone to unlock after reboot). Which workflow is this for? temporary trade-show loaner?
Taylor: temporary 3-day loaner, public booth. need unattended auto-launch on reboot. option 1 sounds better but I thought all company devices had FileVault enforced. is exempting allowed?
kate-kandji: Kandji here 609. Kandji policy enforces FileVault for standard corporate devices. We support exceptions for supervised devices used as kiosks or shared displays. The flow is: supervise the device via Apple Configurator or ABM (Device Enrollment Program), then push a Kandji profile that sets "Disable FileVault Enforcement" for that device and a managed login account with auto-login enabled. We log the exception and put a short expiration on the policy (e.g., 7 days).
alex-sec: security note: exceptions are allowed for limited cases (kiosks, demo devices) with controls: short TTL on exemption, signed audit entry, physical access controls at the booth, and disabling local admin. We don't ship exceptions for user laptops. We also require that the kiosk account is tightly sandboxed (managed app-only) and network egress is locked.
olivia-people: looping in Ops so the loaner is recorded. Taylor i'll add the kiosk exception to your onboarding ticket and confirm pickup/dropoff times.
Taylor: sounds good. Im on-site now and can hand it to IT for supervision. quick question: how do we create the managed auto-login account via CLI so I can test before handing over?
marco-it: we usually create a managed local account (non-admin) via sysadminctl and set the auto-login key in the system plist for supervised devices. Example steps after supervision: ```bash
# create managed user (company-kiosk)
sudo sysadminctl -addUser kioskuser -fullName "Company Kiosk" -password "R3@nch!*tmp" -home /Users/kioskuser -admin no
# mark the account as managed (mdm enrollment will also set this)
# enable auto-login for supervised device by setting the shared Defaults domain (requires MDM push on supervised devices)
sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow autoLoginUser kioskuser
sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow autoLoginUserUID 501
``` Note: the autoLoginUser plist trick only works on supervised devices and is prevented when FileVault is On. Also the password storage is managed by MDM in the supervised flow rather than storing cleartext.```
Taylor: got it. I'm not set up with Apple Configurator — can IT supervise it for me?
marco-it: yes. Bring the device to the IT bench. We'll run Apple Configurator to supervise and enroll to ABM so Kandji sees it as supervised. deploy-bot: supervision session scheduled for marco-it (15m). ticket #ONB-5788.
marco-it: once supervised I'll push the "Kiosk - AutoLogin (supervised)" profile which: creates kioskuser, disables FileVault enforcement, sets auto-login, restricts Launchpad to the kiosk app, and locks down System Preferences. It'll also set a 7-day exemption TTL.
kate-kandji: Kandji will report the device as "supervised" and we will push the keyset change. After that, you should see `sudo fdesetup status` show FileVault: Off (policy-exempt) for that device.
Taylor: ok IT bench now. marco, i'll hand it over in 5.
marco-it: done supervising and pushed profile. Confirming status from my side: Kandji reports device supervised and profile applied. Please run:```bash
$ sudo fdesetup status
FileVault is Off.
Users: kioskuser (Enabled)
Escrow: Not applicable (kiosk-exempt)
```
Taylor: ran it. shows FileVault Off and kioskuser present. I restarted and kiosk app launched on boot automatically. perfect.
alex-sec: recorded the exception in the secure log: exemption ONB-5788, supervised kiosk, TTL 7 days, physical controls required. We'll rotate the kiosk password after the event and reprovision.
olivia-people: added the pickup/dropoff to your onboarding ticket and set reminder to return the device for reprovisioning.
Taylor: thanks everyone. one last q: if the kiosk gets stolen, what's the recovery plan given FileVault is Off?
alex-sec: good question. For supervised kiosk devices we enabled MDM Lost Mode and remote wipe. We also enforce full-disk encryption for all standard laptops; kiosks are the exception and thus treated as higher-risk. If stolen, IT will issue remote wipe and update the exception list. We'll also blacklist the device in ABM so it can't be re-enrolled without recovery.
Taylor: got it. thanks for the quick help and the rundown. I'll return the device next Monday.
marco-it: np. we'll reprovision it when you return and remove the exemption. thanks for flagging early so we didn't try to force FileVault on an auto-login kiosk.
